get.description: Return an unpaginated array of DeviceWorkspace explicitly owned by the authenticated Peer, including system Workspaces. Shared and ownerless Workspaces, and Workspaces whose asynchronous deletion is pending, are excluded. An empty owned set returns []. Workflows are identified only by the collection and RuntimeProfile workflow name that GET /gizclaw/v1/device/runtime-profile lists, resolved against the current RuntimeProfile exactly like Peer RPC Workspace.workflow_name; the Admin Workflow ID is never returned. When the alias no longer resolves, workflow_name is omitted and available is false. Optional collection and workflow_name filters match exactly; a workflow_name filter never matches a Workspace whose alias does not resolve. Uses existing Bearer owner/runtime authorization: 400 INVALID_REQUEST for a malformed public-key bearer, 401 INVALID_API_KEY, 403 DEBUG_ACCESS_FORBIDDEN or API_KEY_OWNER_UNAVAILABLE, 409 for conflicting routing or PEER_PENDING_DELETION when the owner's own deletion is pending, and 500 INTERNAL_ERROR for unavailable services or storage failures. An empty collection or workflow_name filter returns 400 INVALID_REQUEST. Errors use ErrorResponse with error.code and error.message.

delete.description: Start the asynchronous deletion of one Workspace owned by the authenticated Peer, using the same Workspace deletion as Peer RPC server.workspace.delete: the Workspace leaves every list at once, and its history, audio, runtime state and icon are removed in the background. The route never contacts the device. A session that is still running on the Workspace stops when the background cleanup quiesces it; until the cleanup finishes, the device reading the Workspace receives WORKSPACE_PENDING_DELETION and creating another Workspace with the same name returns ALREADY_EXISTS. Foreign, absent, or already pending-deletion Workspace IDs return 404 WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND. A system Workspace returns 409 SYSTEM_WORKSPACE_DELETE_FORBIDDEN, and an owner whose own deletion is pending returns 409 PEER_PENDING_DELETION. Shared Bearer/runtime errors apply; a public-key bearer requires fullcontrol debug mode. Unavailable services or storage failures return 500 INTERNAL_ERROR. Errors use ErrorResponse with error.code and error.message.
delete.summary: Delete a Workspace owned by the authenticated device

202.description: Deletion accepted; cleanup continues in the background.

get.description: Query only the named owned Workspace. Optional limit is 1..200 (default 50); query is literal text with a 512 UTF-8 byte limit. Optional order is desc (default, newest first) or asc (oldest first). Optional start_time_ms (inclusive) and end_time_ms (exclusive) bound created_at in Unix milliseconds; either side may be omitted, so end_time_ms alone jumps to entries before a moment and start_time_ms alone reads entries from a moment onward. History is returned in the requested order as PeerRunHistoryListResponse (available, items, has_next, optional next_cursor). Each item has name (entry ID), type, actor_name, text, created_at, replay_available, and optional gear_id. Cursor is an exclusive entry-ID boundary formatted YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS.nnnnnnnnnZ-suffix: the previous next_cursor to continue in the same order, or any returned item name to page away from that item in the requested order. It is not an authorization token. Time bounds still apply to continuation requests. A well-formed boundary from another stream still queries only this owned Workspace. Malformed cursors return 400 INVALID_HISTORY_CURSOR; invalid query/limit/order or a start_time_ms not before end_time_ms returns 400 INVALID_REQUEST. Foreign or absent Workspace IDs return 404 WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND. Shared Bearer/runtime errors apply. Missing service/history storage or backend failures return 500 INTERNAL_ERROR. ErrorResponse carries error.code and error.message.
get.summary: Read history from a Workspace owned by the authenticated device

get.description: Query the configured persistent system Log Store with required positive start_time_ms and end_time_ms Unix milliseconds, start before end. Optional query is literal text, limited to 512 UTF-8 bytes; level must be exactly DEBUG, INFO, WARN, or ERROR; limit is 1..500 (default 100). Results are newest first: DeviceLogPage contains items (ServerLogEntry: time_ms, level, message, source, path, fields) and end (count, has_next, optional next_cursor). Cursor is an opaque encrypted continuation bound to the same Peer, text, level, time interval and descending order; limit may change. Return 400 INVALID_REQUEST for invalid level/limit/text, INVALID_LOG_QUERY for invalid bounds/filter, INVALID_LOG_CURSOR for malformed cursors or process-local cursors invalidated by a restart, or LOG_CURSOR_MISMATCH for changed query or cross-Peer continuation. Return 500 LOG_QUERY_NOT_CONFIGURED when query_store is absent, or INTERNAL_ERROR for backend failures. Shared Bearer/runtime errors apply. Errors use ErrorResponse with error.code and error.message.
get.summary: Search persistent system logs scoped to the authenticated device

get.description: Read the retained Ogg asset for an entry in an owned Workspace without starting an Agent. A successful 200 response is binary audio/ogg with Content-Length when known; it is not JSON or an unauthenticated URL. Foreign or absent Workspace IDs, missing history entries, or entries without a stored Ogg asset return 404 HISTORY_NOT_FOUND. replay_available alone does not guarantee that Ogg audio exists. Shared Bearer/runtime errors apply; unavailable services or backend failures return 500 INTERNAL_ERROR. ErrorResponse carries error.code and error.message.

get.summary: Get the firmware channels configured for the bound device
get.description: Returns every channel of the Firmware configuration bound to the caller device, read from Server configuration. Reading never contacts the device, so it answers while the device is offline. Channel selection stays with the caller: pick a channel from this response and name it when triggering an update.

200.description: Firmware channels configured for the bound device.

get.summary: Get the RuntimeProfile workflow catalog of the bound device
get.description: Returns the identity of the RuntimeProfile currently bound to the caller device together with its workflow collections and the workflow names in each collection. name and revision equal runtime_profile_name and runtime_profile_revision in Peer RPC responses, and each workflow name is the alias the device uses with server.workflow.*. The response is projected from the RuntimeProfile bindings only and does not check whether the Workflow resource behind a binding still exists: resource bindings, i18n text, drivers, models, voices, memory, pet definitions and app configuration are never returned. Collections and workflows are sorted by name. Reading never contacts the device.

200.description: RuntimeProfile workflow catalog of the bound device.

put.summary: Set the absolute volume and mute state of the bound device
put.description: Forwards client.device.volume.set to the online device and stores the PeerStatus it reports. Equal inputs are idempotent.

200.description: PeerStatus reported by the device after applying the volume.

post.summary: Play a device-defined sound on the bound device
post.description: Forwards client.device.sound.play to the online device. The sound identifier is device-defined; the device validates it and answers DEVICE_REJECTED for unknown sounds.

204.description: The device accepted the playback request.

post.summary: Ring the bound device so it can be found
post.description: Forwards client.device.find to the online device. The device plays its own built-in find-me sound with a rising volume ramp; no audio URL or catalog track is involved. duration_ms is the requested ring time, and the device picks its own default when it is omitted.

204.description: The device accepted the find request.

post.description: Forwards client.device.reboot to the online device. The device acknowledges before rebooting; later control commands answer DEVICE_OFFLINE until the device reconnects.

204.description: The device accepted the reboot request.

post.summary: Notify the bound device to run a firmware update
post.description: Forwards client.firmware.update to the online device. The device acknowledges before it downloads, verifies, and writes the package itself; later control commands answer DEVICE_OFFLINE once it restarts. channel names the channel from GET /gizclaw/v1/device/firmware to install, and defaults to the channel the device already uses. sha256 declares the package the caller saw, and the device rejects the request when it does not match the package it resolves.

204.description: The device accepted the firmware update request.

get.summary: Read the bound device's active Friend invite token
get.description: Same data as server.friend.invite_token.get. Reads the shared Social store and never contacts the device.

404.description: INVITE_TOKEN_NOT_FOUND when the device has no unexpired Friend invite token.

post.summary: Create or return the bound device's Friend invite token
post.description: Without ttl_seconds this is server.friend.invite_token.create: an active token is returned unchanged and a new token lives 5 minutes. With ttl_seconds a new token lives that long, and an active token keeps its value while its expires_at is extended to now + ttl_seconds; it is never shortened. The body may be omitted.

delete.summary: Revoke the bound device's Friend invite token
delete.description: Same as server.friend.invite_token.clear. Idempotent: succeeds when no token exists.

post.description: Same as server.friend.add, except that an already active relationship is reported as FRIEND_ALREADY_EXISTS instead of being returned again. Creates both directions of the relationship and their shared Friend Workspace.

400.description: INVALID_REQUEST when invite_token is empty; FRIEND_SELF_INVITE when the token belongs to the bound device.

404.description: INVITE_TOKEN_INVALID when the invite token does not exist or has expired.

409.description: FRIEND_ALREADY_EXISTS when the two Peers are already Friends; FRIEND_LIMIT_REACHED when either Peer already has 10 Friends; PEER_PENDING_DELETION or PEER_DELETED when the owner or the token's Peer is being retired or is gone.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid, or revoked API key.

Forbidden.description: The API key does not authorize this operation.

NotFound.description: The API key was not found for this owner.

FirmwareNotFound.description: The caller device has no Firmware configuration bound, or the bound configuration no longer exists.

Conflict.description: The API key owner is pending deletion.

DeviceOffline.description: The device has no active connection, or is rebooting and has not reconnected.

DeviceTimeout.description: The device did not answer within the control timeout.

DeviceUnsupported.description: The device does not implement this control method.

FriendGroupNotFound.description: FRIEND_GROUP_NOT_FOUND when the bound device has no Friend Group with this name. Group names are per member, so a non-member never resolves another member's name.

FriendGroupMemberNotFound.description: FRIEND_GROUP_NOT_FOUND when the bound device has no Friend Group with this name; FRIEND_GROUP_MEMBER_NOT_FOUND when the Peer is not a member.

FriendGroupForbidden.description: FRIEND_GROUP_PERMISSION_DENIED when the bound device's role in the Group does not permit the operation; API_KEY_OWNER_UNAVAILABLE or DEBUG_ACCESS_FORBIDDEN from bearer validation.

FriendGroupConflict.description: FRIEND_GROUP_CHANGED on a concurrent change (retry); FRIEND_GROUP_PENDING_DELETION when the Group is being deleted; PEER_PENDING_DELETION or PEER_DELETED when a Peer is being retired or is gone.

DeviceError.description: The device answered with an unexpected RPC error.

BearerAuth.description: API key gizclaw_sk_v1_<secret>, or gizclaw_pk_<canonical Base58 public key> for device debug access. Public-key bearer access requires the authoritative Server runtime mode to permit the operation. Raw public keys and query selectors are not supported.
